portal_hypertension.abstract: This report describes initial clinical experience using the 6- to 10-mm GORE VIATORR transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt (TIPS) Endoprosthesis with Controlled Expansion (W. L. Gore & Associates, Inc.) for reduction of established TIPS. Four patients underwent TIPS reduction for medically refractory hepatic encephalopathy (n=3) or progressive pulmonary hypertension (n=1). A new 6- to 10-mm VIATORR stent was deployed within the existing TIPS and was dilated using a 6 mm balloon in two patients or left without post-placement balloon dilation in two patients. portal_hypertension.abstract: A 59-year-old woman presented with recurrent hematemesis and generalized weakness. Imaging revealed a giant high-flow arteriovenous shunt between markedly dilated splenic arterial and venous systems, associated with an 8 × 5 cm splenic arterial aneurysmal component, portal hypertension, and gastric fundal varices. Angiography demonstrated high flow through markedly dilated vessels, precluding safe endovascular embolization. The patient underwent open splenectomy with complete excision of the vascular lesion, achieving full symptom resolution and complete resolution of gastric varices at 6-month follow-up. portal_hypertension.abstract: There has been a recent surge in interest in portal vein thrombosis (PVT), as evidenced by the increase in publications on this topic, along with heterogeneity in the terminology, classification, and management of this disorder. The Indian National Association for Study of the Liver vascular liver disease task force, with extensive expertise in portal hypertension, along with other invited experts actively working in this field, has formulated a consensus guideline on the definition, nomenclature, epidemiology, clinical features, natural history, diagnosis, and management of PVT using evidence from published literature.
